claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation of high-entropy-alloy bond coats forms an alumina scale.
The pre-oxidation-induced alumina scale is coherent and dense.
The alumina scale enhances oxide adherence and delays degradation.
Controlled pre-oxidation improves the durability and reliability of the thermal barrier coating.
Heating at approximately 1050 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere for a controlled duration can produce a uniform, adherent alumina layer on the bond-coat surface.
The pre-oxidation treatment produces a thin, continuous, and adherent alumina scale.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress.
The alumina scale mitigates oxide spallation at elevated temperatures.
Pre-oxidation drives selective alumina formation on the high-entropy-alloy bond-coat surface.
The engineered alumina interface reduces subsequent oxidation rates.
The engineered alumina interface reduces thermal stress at the coating–substrate interface.
Reduced oxidation and interfacial thermal stress extend the coating's operational lifetime.
Pre-oxidation is predicted to increase lifetime or time to spallation by approximately 30% relative to untreated bond coats under cyclic high-temperature conditions.
Untreated high-entropy-alloy bond coats undergo conventional oxide-scale growth that leads to earlier spallation and degradation.
The beneficial effect should persist during standard high-temperature cyclic oxidation and thermal-shock exposure, including cycles near 1100 °C in oxidizing atmospheres.
The benefit may not persist under extreme thermal gradients, unusual gas compositions, or very high humidity because different degradation mechanisms may prevail.
